```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 5, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE)
```

## Question, source and sampling unit

Harbour seal scat samples provide evidence of which prey groups were detected
by DNA metabarcoding. Here we describe those detections, compare their relative
DNA signal across sample groups and examine the resolution of taxonomic
assignments. The analysis is descriptive. It does not estimate consumed
biomass or establish seasonal or laboratory effects.

We use the published `salish_seal_dna` data of Thomas et al. (2022):
4,625 harbour seal (*Phoca vitulina*) scats from 52 Salish Sea haul-outs,
2012–2018. Each row is a prey assignment **within one scat**. This is a secondary
analysis of the published taxon-level dataset, **not** a rerun of the
raw-sequence pipeline. The released `diet_fraction` is an already
calculated within-scat DNA fraction, combining
information from 16S and COI markers. The frozen WoRMS taxonomy,
`salish_seal_lineage`, avoids live API lookups. The data source and CC0 status
are documented in `?salish_seal_dna`.

**Unit:** one `sample_id` (scat). **Taxon key:** `prey_label`. **Quantity:**
`diet_fraction`, *not* prey grams. **Covariates:** site, year, season and lab.

```{r data}
library(DietView)
dat <- salish_seal_dna
lin <- salish_seal_lineage
c(records = nrow(dat), scats = length(unique(dat$sample_id)),
  prey_labels = length(unique(dat$prey_label)), sites = length(unique(dat$site)))
head(dat[, c("sample_id", "prey_label", "diet_fraction", "season", "lab")])
```

## Audit the input before analysis

A fraction should be finite, non-negative and, in these released data, sum to
approximately one **within each positive scat**. These checks are diagnostic:
they should not be used to silently remove unexpected values.

```{r audit}
stopifnot(!anyNA(dat$sample_id), !anyNA(dat$prey_label))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(dat$diet_fraction)), all(dat$diet_fraction >= 0))
scat_total <- tapply(dat$diet_fraction, dat$sample_id, sum)
summary(scat_total)
max(abs(scat_total - 1))
```

```{r sample-frame}
frame <- unique(dat[, c("sample_id", "site", "year", "season", "lab")])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(frame$sample_id))
print(table(frame$season, useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(frame$lab, useNA = "ifany"))
```

**Interpretation.** `frame` counts scats, not prey records. Samples can contain
several prey detections. Without a complete list of *all scats processed* we
cannot calculate a survey-wide negative-detection or extraction-failure rate:
these released rows describe the samples represented in the published table.

## Specify roles and freeze the taxonomy

`weight_type = "rra"` asks DietView to normalize the quantity within each
sample. Here the original fractions are already normalized; applying this
operation again is effectively idempotent (apart from numeric rounding). For
**raw** ASV read counts, the same argument first performs the normalization;
see the separate [ASV case study](case-study-asv-pipeline.html).

```{r prepare}
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator = "predator", stomach = "sample_id", prey_name = "prey_label",
  weight = "diet_fraction", weight_type = "rra", unit_label = "scat",
  covariates = c("site", "year", "season", "lab")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin,
                   verbose = FALSE)
prep
c(raw_quantity = "diet_fraction", normalized_column = prep$spec$weight)
```

```{r verify-normalization}
normalized <- tapply(prep$data[[prep$spec$weight]], prep$data$sample_id, sum)
summary(normalized)
stopifnot(all(abs(normalized[scat_total > 0] - 1) < 1e-6))
```

The frozen classification retains the *shared* ranks for ambiguous assignments
such as two alternative rockfish species, instead of choosing one arbitrarily.
A prey label with more than one candidate is not a precise species
identification.

```{r ambiguity}
head(lin[lin$n_candidates > 1,
         c("prey_label", "family", "genus", "species", "n_candidates")])
```

## Describe the sample before the diet

```{r summary}
dv_summary(prep, by = "season")
```

The numbers describe this **collection of scats**, not a random sample of
all seal feeding in the Salish Sea. Seasonal contrasts are confounded by site,
year, laboratory and collection effort unless the design is addressed.

## Calculate three different measures

The three columns below measure **different** things. `pct_occ` is the share
of *taxon–scat records*; it is not frequency of occurrence. `pct_w` is the
sample-normalized **relative DNA read signal**. `pct_fo` is the proportion of
represented scats in which a taxon was detected, at the requested rank.

```{r family}
tree <- dv_tree(prep)
family <- dv_rank_table(tree, "Family")
head(family[order(-family$pct_w),
            c("label", "value_occ", "pct_occ", "pct_w")], 10)
```

```{r occurrence}
fo <- dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "family", denominator = "nonempty")
head(fo[order(-fo$pct_fo), c("taxon", "n_stomachs", "n_total", "pct_fo")], 10)
```

At each taxonomic rank, DietView retains an unidentified category. A family
label `NA` may occur beneath *different* parent taxa; use the hierarchy when
reading such cells rather than combining their labels indiscriminately.

```{r rank-conservation}
ranks <- unique(as.character(tree$rank))
totals <- vapply(ranks, function(r) {
  x <- tree[tree$rank == r, ]
  sum(x$pct_w)
}, numeric(1))
round(totals, 6)
stopifnot(all(abs(totals - 100) < 1e-4))
```

## Render and interpret a real interactive figure

```{r plot-dna}
dv_sunburst(tree, mode = "weight",
            title = "Harbour seal scats: relative DNA signal by sample",
            subtitle = "Mean RRA, not prey biomass")
```

Read the rings from coarse to fine. Each ring partitions the same normalized
DNA signal, with white segments for material not identified below a particular
rank. A large wedge says **more DNA signal in these samples**, not necessarily
more prey individuals, biomass or energy. Marker efficiency, primer bias,
digestion, reference-library coverage and laboratory methods all matter.

## Identification resolution and stratification

```{r resolution}
res <- dv_resolution(prep, by = "lab")
head(res[, c("lab", "finest_rank", "n_records", "p_records", "p_weight")], 12)
```

As a descriptive comparison, prepare two sample-level strata from the frozen
data. Do not interpret unadjusted contrasts as ecological trends.

```{r strata}
season_sizes <- sort(table(frame$season), decreasing = TRUE)
season_sizes
major <- names(season_sizes)[seq_len(min(2L, length(season_sizes)))]
season_tables <- lapply(major, function(s) {
  ds <- dat[!is.na(dat$season) & as.character(dat$season) == s, ]
  ps <- dv_prepare(ds, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin,
                   verbose = FALSE)
  tb <- dv_rank_table(dv_tree(ps), "Family")
  data.frame(season = s, tb[, c("label", "pct_w")])
})
head(do.call(rbind, season_tables), 12)
```

## Export data and prepare a dashboard

`dv_matrix()` produces a **scat-by-taxon** numeric matrix for downstream
analysis; rows are scats, not repeated prey records. The `weight` currency
contains sample-normalized proportions here.

```{r matrix}
m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "weight")
c(samples = nrow(m), families_and_unidentified = ncol(m))
head(round(rowSums(m), 5))
```

```{r export}
export <- file.path(tempdir(), "salish_seal_family_rra.csv")
utils::write.csv(m, export, row.names = TRUE)
file.exists(export)
```

Build a single-file HTML dashboard **on your own computer**. This optional
step is not run while the vignette is built, since it writes a second large
HTML file; run it interactively when you want to share the result.

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "salish_seal_dna_dashboard.html"),
  bands = c("occurrence", "weight"), strata = c("season", "lab"),
  min_stomachs = 25,
  title = "Harbour seal DNA composition: Salish Sea (descriptive)")
```

## Reporting and interpretation

Report the source, license, date, marker and laboratory, sampling unit,
preprocessing, unique sample count **per stratum**, treatment of ambiguous
taxa, classification version, metric/denominator, and exclusions. In a
scientific study, add sampling-design-aware uncertainty intervals and evaluate
batch, site and year effects. Do not equate DNA reads or RRA to biomass or
individual consumption; a detection in a scat is not proof of a particular
meal size. This vignette describes detection patterns, not causal or
population-level seasonal changes.

**References:** Thomas et al. (2022), *Scientific Data* 9:68,
<https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01152-5> (data CC0);
Deagle et al. (2019), *Molecular Ecology* 28:391–406,
<https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.14734>.
